revision: not recorded here — a manifest cannot name the commit that contains it, for the same reason it cannot contain its own hash. The release identity is version + revision + digest: two are in-tree, and the consuming project records the revision in its own pin and verifies with `pack_pin.py <root> --version <v> --sha <full-40-char-rev> --digest <d> --state <state>`. See docs/RP2.2-GATE.md.
digest_note: release-local framing. Verify a release with the tools/pack_pin.py that ships inside it; a manifest naming an algorithm the verifier does not implement fails as a version mismatch, not as tampering.
supersedes: 2.2.0 — not replaced; runs pinned to it stay pinned to it. 2.2.0, 2.1.1, 2.1.0 and 2.0.0 histories are untouched. This candidate is IN_PROGRESS and no project may adopt it: QUALIFIED_AND_FROZEN is the only adoptable state.
version_semantics: PATCH: backward-compatible fixes, metadata/docs corrections, enforcement of already-promised guarantees. MINOR: new backward-compatible policy/tool/capability. MAJOR: incompatible authority, contract or migration change. VERSION is the single machine-readable authority (DECISIONS.md D11).
pin_instruction: a project records ROOT PATH and version and full 40-character sha and tree digest and state in PROJECT.yaml pack.*, and verifies them rather than copying them. All four identity fields are required: `root_path` says WHICH DIRECTORY, the other three say WHAT is in it, and a pin without the root is UNVERIFIABLE_LEGACY_PIN (tools/pack_migration.py) because the release it names cannot be identified. Adoption happens only at a capability boundary. A frozen release never mutates during a project run; verification failing mid-project is a stop, not a pin to refresh.
concurrent_use: several projects may pin this same release at once, or different qualified releases, provided each version resolves to a distinct immutable root. Operational state and Evolution Candidate inboxes are project-local and never written into this repository (DECISIONS.md D13).

external_installed_skills.authority: ADAPTERS, NOT AUTHORITY. Outside this release envelope, covered by no tree_digest_sha256, and changeable without a pin noticing. Where an adapter and this pinned pack disagree, the pinned pack wins. From 2.2.0 an adapter a project dispatches through is DECLARED AND VERIFIED under the project's own adapters contract (tools/adapter_pin.py, PROJECT.yaml `adapters:`) — this list is an observation of what was installed here, never a substitute for that declaration (DECISIONS.md D12, D14).

known_limitations: STATE IS IN_PROGRESS. This is a candidate, not a release. No project may pin it, and moving it to QUALIFIED_AND_FROZEN is a human decision (policy/hitl-matrix.md row 2) the coordinator does not take.

THEY ARE UNADJUDICATED, and by this release's own rule a bare count is not a remediation list. The largest contributors are PACK_MANIFEST.json (259), CHANGELOG.md (186), docs/RP2.2-GATE.md (134) and policy/observations.jsonl (131) — this repository IS the denylist and its records discuss the vocabulary, which is the case skills/core/public-safety.md describes when it says a project whose product is a harness cannot scan its own source for harness vocabulary. the tree digest is computed over WORKING-TREE BYTES, so a checkout with core.autocrlf=true produces a different digest for the same commit. There is no .gitattributes.

ROUND 1 RETURNED NOT READY ON BOTH LENSES. Two blind auditors, one cross-vendor on an independent pool: 5 blockers and 3 major from the falsification lens, 2 blockers and 5 major from the release-authority lens, findings almost disjoint. Every one reproduced by execution before repair; fifteen repaired. THE REPAIRS MADE AFTER A VERDICT ARE THEMSELVES UNAUDITED until the delta re-audit recorded in the gate record, which is the standing condition of any final repair. ROUND 2, the bounded delta re-audit, returned NOT READY on five blockers — THREE OF THEM DEFECTS IN ROUND 1'S REPAIRS — plus four recommendations and six tests named as decorative. All reproduced and all repaired. The round-2 repairs are themselves unaudited until the next delta check, which is the standing condition of any final repair. ROUND 3, a blind cross-vendor read, returned NOT READY on eight findings — SIX OF WHICH WERE ALREADY REPAIRED, because the auditor read a snapshot two rounds old and its report did not state the revision. Two were real and are repaired. The stale-evidence problem is closed in the gate rather than in the brief alone. ROUND 4, the blind cross-vendor release-authority read of the candidate itself, returned NOT READY on six blockers, two majors and two minors — including a read-only Git interface that ran the subject repository's own configured program on every diff. All ten reproduced, all ten repaired. Its report opened with the revision and digest it read, so nothing had to be re-executed to learn which tree it meant. ROUND 5, a bounded cross-vendor delta re-audit of round 4's repairs, returned NOT READY on seven findings — FOUR OF THEM DEFECTS IN THE REPAIRS IT WAS SENT TO CHECK, including two further routes by which a read-only Git surface ran the subject's own code. All repaired. Round 5's repairs are themselves unaudited until the next delta check, which is the standing condition of any final repair and is why the closure ceiling was raised rather than reached. ROUND 6 was terminated mid-run by its provider's content filter and wrote no report; FIVE REAL FINDINGS WERE RECOVERED FROM ITS STDERR, including a fourth route by which a repository being read chose a program to run — this one through the transport exception, and closable only by narrowing that exception, because the config key cannot be neutralised from the environment. All five repaired. Round 6 did not complete its sweep, so its coverage is partial by construction. ROUND 7, a blind cross-vendor property read, returned NOT READY on eight findings plus a test that passed with its subject deleted — including a FIFTH route by which a repository being read chose a program to run, this one inside the transport exception itself. All reproduced and all repaired; one finding was examined and kept as designed, with its disclosure sharpened rather than its verdict changed. ROUND 8, the last authorised cycle, was ALSO terminated by its provider's content filter with a zero-byte report; four probes were recovered from its stderr and three were real, including two defects in the class-level defence that had replaced five route-by-route patches. Round 8 did not complete its sweep, so its coverage is partial by construction, and its own repairs are unaudited: the closure ceiling is reached and a ninth reading is a human decision under row 8. CYCLE 9, authorised by the founder specifically to audit round 8's repairs, returned NOT READY on five properties plus a test that could not fail — the first being that round 8's own commit-message repair was broken three ways. All reproduced, all repaired, five mutants killed. Cycle 9's repairs are themselves unaudited, and a tenth reading is a new scoped HITL. CYCLE 10, the last authorised reading, returned NOT READY on nine properties plus two tests that could not fail — including a premise whose command FAILED reporting as reproduced, and a SHA-256 repository scanning clean. All reproduced, all repaired, eight mutants killed. Three findings are declared rather than closed and are listed separately below. CYCLE 11, the delta-bounded final reading, returned NOT READY on five properties — one of which FALSIFIED A BOUND STATED IN THE SAME RELEASE: a forged bundle header produced an unsafe ANCHORED. All reproduced and repaired; three of four mutants survived first run because those repairs had no regression behind them, and all four die now. CYCLE 12, the final correctness closure, returned NOT READY on three defects plus two of the coordinator's own tests that were not evidence. All reproduced and repaired; the mutants that matter were killed, and two ill-formed mutants that changed an assertion rather than its subject were re-run against the subject.

THE CAPACITY GATE HAS NEVER BEEN RUN AGAINST A LIVE PROVIDER READING. Every fixture supplies its own pool figures, and the one documented resource surface this pack can read (tools/resource_observation.py) reports UNKNOWN in the ordinary case by that surface's own definition. What is exercised is the arithmetic, the refusals and the conservative posture; what is not is whether a real reading arrives in the shape the gate expects.

THE DIAGNOSTIC PROJECTION SHIPS AGAINST THE EVIDENCE, ON A HUMAN DECISION. The reconciliation this release draws on refuses a dashboard in terms — a human wanting one is not evidence that Core should ship one — and the refusal is recorded rather than reversed. What answers its concrete objection is the ordering: coordinator state is derived rather than stored, so there is no stored value to go stale. It is a one-shot renderer with no port, no cache and no importer, and removing it is deleting one file.

A REAL PROJECT ON THIS MACHINE STILL CARRIES A PRE-2.1 CONTRACT and this release does not migrate it. The refusal now names the schema generation and the migration instead of reporting a type error, which is the repair; performing the migration is the project's, because the two private-term tiers differ in whether a term applies to blob content and choosing would change what gets scanned.

A CLOSE ATTESTATION DOES NOT VERIFY THAT A PROFILE RAN. The outcomes are supplied by the caller and the state is derived from the exit status the caller records; a caller that records a falsehood records a falsehood. What the mechanism makes impossible is SILENCE — a declared profile cannot be absent from the record. An earlier draft of the module's headline promised independent verification of what ran, which it does not provide; an independent auditor found the sentence and it is corrected rather than left standing.

A DESTROYED CITATION IS DETECTED BY LENGTH, NOT BY PROVENANCE. A forty-character object name this repository does not have is treated as a citation of something gone, and a shorter one as prose. That boundary is a judgement about how people write records, not a fact about Git: a forty-character token that never was a revision would be reported as destroyed. The alternative — treating every unrecognised hexadecimal word as a lost commit — produces a remediation list nobody can act on, which is the failure the adjacent publication work exists to prevent.

THE FAILURE-MODE CLOSURE MATRIX IS THE RELEASE'S OWN CLAIM AND IS NOT INDEPENDENTLY AUDITED AS A WHOLE. Each row cites a test or a rehearsal that can be run, and the auditors of round 1 exercised many of them individually, but no auditor has been asked to falsify the matrix as a document. Its five open residues are stated in it rather than in a summary.

THE PACK'S OWN COMPLETE HISTORY HAS 253 UNADJUDICATED OCCURRENCES. The capability that reads it ships in this release and had never been run over this history before. Re-run after the scanner learned to read ref names and annotated tag messages: 253 occurrences over 1179 objects and ZERO UNSCANNED, so the finding list is now known to be the whole finding list. No personal path or real credential is among them — verified directly, and this evolution's own commits introduce none — but individual adjudication has not been performed, and it is the input to a publication decision rather than a substitute for one. Remediating any historical object is a rewrite: HITL rows 2 and 4.

A PATH-BASED WAIT CANNOT NAME A PRODUCER. An unrelated writer satisfies a PATH_EXISTS or EXIT_FILE wait, and no property of a bare filesystem path distinguishes who wrote it. The observation is strengthened as far as a filesystem permits — a regular file that does not predate its own wait — and OUTPUT_ROOT, whose owner marker is now checked on read as well as on write, is the kind that establishes a producer. A test pins both halves.

THE PROJECTION IS A READER AND HAS NEVER BEEN WATCHED DURING A REAL MULTI-HOUR RUN. It now renders as a page as well as as text, and both were falsified against twelve synthetic states, but nobody has yet watched either during a long run. Its fields are exercised against fixtures and against this session's own live record, where it correctly reported a stale record and an undeclared audit subject. Whether the information architecture is the right one for someone watching a Consumer-A run for six hours is not established, and cannot be until someone does.

THE PROGRAM-VALUED CONFIG LIST IS NOT COMPLETE AND CANNOT BE. It enumerates the shapes of Git config keys whose value is executed; Git may add another, and a key that matches no shape is not inspected. What the design buys is that an unrecognised key MATCHING a shape refuses rather than waiting to be found — the population of routes is open-ended and the population of shapes is smaller and slower-moving, not closed. It also costs two extra Git processes per repository per invocation, about 17 seconds on a 110-second suite.

ONE MECHANISM IS DEFERRED RATHER THAN COVERED: contract, classification and sandbox gaps, inherited from 2.2.0 with no discriminating oracle demonstrated in this release. Recurrence is bounded because the 2.2.0 contract checks ship unchanged and their tests still run, but that is inheritance rather than a demonstration made here, and the final evidence-closure check reclassified it rather than let it read as covered.

A FILESYSTEM CLONE DEFEATS THE CHUNK LINK-COUNT CHECK. `cp -c` on APFS puts one task's bytes in another's root with st_nlink == 1 on both, and nothing on disk distinguishes that from bytes the second task wrote. The ownership guarantee rests on the owner marker and the completion marker, both of which are checked; it does not rest on the bytes. Found by an independent reader in cycle 10, declared rather than closed, and now stated as a bounded guarantee with an oracle: what IS guaranteed is that two roots are never confused, which was executed and holds; what is not is that a root's bytes were computed by its owner. The error cannot cause unsafe acceptance.

THE CHUNK LINK-COUNT CHECK HAS A FALSE POSITIVE: a task that hard-links its own product into its own root classifies UNKNOWN. Wrong in the safe direction — UNKNOWN loses nothing, because `resume_plan` refuses to act on it — and recorded rather than narrowed.

`_bundle_contains` COMPARES BUNDLE TIPS ONLY, so a commit reachable inside a verified bundle but not named as a head reports UNREACHABLE. Safe direction: it blocks where it should anchor. Proving reachability inside a bundle means unbundling, and this release does not write.

THE ARTIFACT GUARDS COST ABOUT 60 SECONDS OF THE SUITE'S 171. `test_every_oracle_the_matrix_names_selects_at_least_one_test` spawns one pytest collection per matrix row, which spawn one pytest collection per matrix row and per recurrence class. Recorded because a check whose cost nobody measured is a check somebody eventually disables, and because the alternative — trusting that the selectors still match — is what it exists to replace.

A BUNDLE CANNOT ANCHOR ANYTHING IN THIS RELEASE. Establishing that a bundle carries a commit means indexing its pack, which is a write, so a verified bundle whose header names a cited commit yields ANCHOR_UNCONFIRMED and BLOCKS. That is strictly more conservative than 2.2.0's behaviour and it is a real cost: a project that anchors closures in bundles will find those closures blocked until a person adjudicates them. Revisit when a read-only way to enumerate a pack's objects is available, or when the write is authorised for a scratch index.

AN ORACLE SELECTING A TEST DOES NOT PROVE IT TESTS THE MECHANISM IT IS CITED FOR. The matrix guard establishes that every citation resolves to something that runs, which is strictly weaker than relevance. Relevance is a human judgement and no check here makes it; the citations were chosen by the coordinator and read by nobody else.

THE INFORMATION ARCHITECTURE IS FROZEN AND NO VISUAL IDENTITY IS CHOSEN. The structural pass set hierarchy, grouping, disclosure and responsive behaviour; colour is functional only, one hue per tone, and no type or palette decision was made for its own sake. The previews exist so that decision can be taken by looking.

THE DASHBOARD HAS NEVER BEEN WATCHED DURING A REAL MULTI-HOUR RUN. Both renderers are falsified against twelve states, two themes and two viewports, and against this session's own live record. Whether the information architecture is right for somebody four hours into a Consumer-A run is not established and cannot be until someone is.
